messages:
alex: FYI customer acme-inc reporting huge latency and auth oddities. They claim Dedicated pool pinned to us-west-2 but responses are coming from hosted in eu-west-1. Ticket #5231 opened :grimacing:

marta: can you paste the request headers / routing ids?

alex: Pasting minimal repro and routing headers:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-redacted
X-Region-Pin: us-west-2
X-Model: redwood-13b
X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
```
Response headers: `X-Serving-Pool: hosted-eu-west-1`, `X-Billing-Route: hosted`. Response time ~ 1.2s vs expected ~80ms.

sam: grabbing routing service logs for req_0a1b2c3d, snippet: 
```
2026-03-01T15:02:12Z route_eval req_0a1b2c3d policy=pin->region evaluated=true
2026-03-01T15:02:12Z route_eval reason=capacity_tag_mismatch pool=dedicated-usw2-42 marked=degraded
2026-03-01T15:02:12Z fallback select hosted eu-west-1 score=0.12 latency_metric=35ms
2026-03-01T15:02:12Z selected hosted-eu-west-1
```

sam: note the weird bit: why eu-west-1? the customer pinned us-west-2.

jess: quick summary after initial triage: autoscaler failed to report healthy nodes for dedicated-usw2-42 for ~45s because the leader goroutine was stuck during a GC, so the pool was transiently flagged degraded. Fallback logic then ran and selected a hosted region by global score. The selection algorithm currently does not constrain fallback regions to the same region as the pin — it ranks by global latency/health and picks top host. That produces cross-region fallbacks.

marta: that explains the latency, but customer also shows billing hits on hosted usage even though they have reserved capacity — that's a big contract breach.

billing: we see hosted token charges for org_8a3f during window 2026-03-01T15:02:00Z-15:05:00Z: charge ids ch_7a6b. We're putting a hold and will prepare a refund/credit, but need eng confirmation the routing was incorrect.

alex: customer repro steps we gave them: run this curl 3x quickly (one will hit hosted):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-redacted' \
  -H 'X-Region-Pin: us-west-2' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hello"}' -D - | sed -n '1,20p'
```
Include `X-Request-Id` and we can track.

jess: mitigation plan: (1) short-term patch: change routing policy so that when a request includes X-Region-Pin, fallback candidates are filtered to same region OR same region-group (e.g., us-west-*). I'll open an urgent PR to routing-service to enforce region affinity for pinned requests. (2) medium-term: add clearer telemetry when pool degradation is due to stale health vs true capacity shortfall. (3) long-term: autoscaler leader fix and a circuit that prevents marking pool degraded for <60s transient faults.

sam: PR #9012 opened: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pulls/9012 - adds affinity filter and test. Rolling a canary now.

ops-bot: deploy started: routing-service rev=cb2a3 (canary) -> 2 nodes in us-west-2, 2 nodes in eu-west-1.

marta: customer wants SLA explanation + refund. Support to coordinate messaging: apologize, explain fallback, confirm patching plan and ETA for rollback/monitoring.

support-bot: created escalation ticket ESCL-1278 assigned to eng-runtime + billing.

alex: quick ask for eng-runtime: can you validate there are no other code paths that choose a geographically distant hosted fallback when a region pin exists? We need to be sure fix is exhaustive.

jess: checking now. Early scan: three places call into select_hosted_candidate(). Two call sites already pass region_hint; third didn't. I'll add a guard and an integration test covering pinned requests and simulated transient health outages. ETA for PR merge: 2 hours; canary metrics expected within 10m of merge.

billing: put credit hold on ch_7a6b and draft note for support to send once engineer confirms.

alex: sending customer this interim message: "We've identified a routing fallback issue that caused your pinned requests to be served from hosted eu-west-1 during a transient health signal. We're rolling a fix to restrict fallbacks to your pinned region and will credit hosted usage during the incident window. Apologies for the latency and surprise billing — we'll follow up with timeline." :pray:

marta: keep this thread updated with canary metrics. If canary shows any regression, we revert.

sam: canary looks clean so far: p95 latency for pinned requests back to ~75ms within 6m of rollout. No additional hosted hits observed in test window.

jess: merged and promoted to stable. Routing-service rev cb2a3 -> stable.

ops-bot: deploy succeeded: routing-service rev cb2a3 promoted to stable in us-west-2, eu-west-1.

billing: refund applied for ch_7a6b and customer credited account with 5000 token credit.

alex: closing loop with customer now. Will paste final note from support here when sent.

marta: final support note sent at 2026-03-01T16:04Z. Customer accepted credit, asked for a postmortem. Assign to eng-runtime for write-up.

sam: adding postmortem board item.

jess: filing a short RFC for region-affinity fallback as product-configurable option.

support-bot: thread archived after customer confirmation.
